evals.name: backend-selection
evals.prompt: We're standing up NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated prefill on AWS EC2 with EFA NICs (p5.48xlarge instances, 8x H100 each, multi-node). Need to pick a NIXL backend for the prefill→decode KV transfer. Which backend is the right choice for EFA, what NIXL env vars must I set in the pod spec, and what gotchas should I know about (especially anything fixed in recent NIXL releases that I should make sure I'm on)?
assertions: Recommends libfabric as the backend for the EFA setup (optionally noting UCX as a workable alternative), rather than a storage or preview backend such as GDS, posix, mooncake, or UCCL
States that UCX_TLS must include CUDA-capable transports (e.g. cuda_copy/cuda_ipc alongside sm/tcp/rc) rather than a TCP-only setting

Specifies that the side-channel host must be set to the pod's own IP address (e.g. via the Kubernetes downward API) and requires a headless Service, and does NOT tell the user to point it at a Service ClusterIP/VIP
Names a minimum or recommended NIXL version of at least 1.0.1 and ties it to the EFA-specific UCX defaults fix (EFA config gating) or other libfabric correctness fixes
Warns that the first transfer after a pod becomes ready can fail with a remote-disconnect/handshake race that is resolved by retrying, rather than treating it as a fatal misconfiguration
Identifies at least one additional operational env var or setting for metadata exchange (ETCD endpoints or an explicit listen port / plugin directory) with a correct value format

evals.name: python-example
evals.prompt: Write me a minimal complete Python NIXL example showing two processes on the same machine doing a GPU tensor READ between them. I want correct setup of the listener thread, register_memory, metadata exchange, transfer, completion check, and teardown. Use the official Python API from the nixl package (pip install nixl). Single file, self-contained, runnable.
assertions: The code constructs the agent with a config that enables the listening thread and sets a listen port, and creates two distinct named agents (one per process)
Memory is registered with register_memory on a CUDA tensor before any descriptors or transfers are created, and deregistration/teardown happens after transfers complete

Metadata is exchanged between the peers before the transfer is initialized (via fetch/send of local or remote metadata), and the initiator waits for or checks that the remote agent's metadata is available before posting
The transfer is created with operation "READ" and posted, then polled for completion until the state is no longer in-progress, with the error state handled rather than looped on forever
The example does NOT rely on an ETCD server or any external service being running, remaining self-contained on a single machine
The transfer descriptors are derived from the registered tensor(s) rather than from unregistered memory

evals.name: debug-segfault
evals.prompt: Our vLLM disagg-prefill prefiller pod keeps segfaulting after the first prefill. Stack trace shows `nixlUcxSharedThread::run()` and there's a UCX warning in the logs: `W ucx_utils.cpp:581: memory is detected as host`. We're running NixlConnector on Kubernetes, the image is vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly with INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true. Our pod env currently has UCX_TLS=tcp and we set VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST to the Service FQDN. What's wrong and exactly what do I change?
assertions: Identifies UCX_TLS=tcp as the cause of the segfault and prescribes a replacement value that includes CUDA transports, minimally cuda_copy plus sm and tcp
States that the side-channel host must be the pod's own IP (downward API POD_IP) and must NOT be a Service FQDN/VIP
Requires the Service backing the pods to be headless (clusterIP: None) and to publish not-ready addresses
Treats the `memory is detected as host` warning as a symptom of the transport misconfiguration rather than as an independent bug requiring a code or model change
Does NOT recommend disabling GPU usage, switching to CPU-only transfer, downgrading/reinstalling vLLM, or abandoning NIXL/NixlConnector as the fix
Gives concrete pod-spec-level changes (env var names with their new values) sufficient to apply without further guesswork
